Be skeptical when Cowork plus the Chrome integration proposes
an unexpected action. If you asked Claude to search for information on
a website and Claude suddenly proposes to download a file or modify a
document, pause and ask yourself whether that action aligns with what
you requested. Unexpected proposals are a sign that Claude may have
encountered malicious content.

Do not grant Cowork broad access to emails from unknown
senders. If you use Cowork's email integration, limit which email folders
Claude can access and from whom. A compromise in email permissions
is a straight line to credential exfiltration or account takeover.
Watch for unexpected patterns in Claude's behavior. Is Claude
accessing files or websites you did not mention? Is it asking for unusual
permissions? Is it repeating the same action multiple times? These
patterns can signal that Claude has encountered embedded instructions
and is following them.

Files were modified or deleted unexpectedly
Stop the task immediately and assess what changed. If the project

git, check your backup. For the future: before granting Claude access to
any folder, back it up, and use a dedicated working folder rather than
giving Claude access to directories containing irreplaceable files.
